sections.title: For people who help adults learn
sections.blurb: Curricula, kits, and training for tutors, teachers, and program staff.

sections.title: Running a program
sections.blurb: Help for starting, strengthening, and sustaining a program, whether you are paid staff or a volunteer team.

sections.title: Funding
sections.blurb: Grants and free tools for programs. Eligibility and dates change, so check each one before you plan around it.

sections.title: For adults who are learning
sections.blurb: Free tools you can use on your own, at your own pace, on your phone or a computer.

resources.title: Pathway to Literacy
resources.description: A free, well-rounded curriculum and assessment tool for adult learners with emerging literacy. Includes a 10-week sequence organized into four levels (A to D), a reading diagnostic, and an intake assessment.

note.label: What we love about it
note.text: With everything hosted in Google Slides, this resource is easy to access and use.

resources.title: ESL Instructional Support Kits
resources.description: A set of five free, downloadable kits: Pronunciation, Phonics and Phonemic Awareness, Speaking and Listening, Reading, and Citizenship. Each is packed with grab-and-go activities for one-on-one, small group, or full class settings.

note.label: What we love about it
note.text: Grab-and-go activities that actually work. Low prep, high utility.

resources.title: CILIA-T
resources.source: University of Minnesota Duluth / Literacy Minnesota
resources.description: A comprehensive, research-backed curriculum for intermediate and advanced adult English language learners, focused on academic vocabulary, comprehension, and digital literacy skills.

note.label: What we love about it
note.text: It pushes learners toward the academic language needed for higher education, career advancement, and citizenship. Rigorous and free.

resources.title: Phonemic Awareness in Older Learners: Bridging the Gap
resources.description: A free on-demand webinar exploring how phonemic awareness instruction can be a game-changer for older students and adult learners who struggle with word reading. Educators can earn a free CE certificate upon completion.

note.label: What we love about it
note.text: Phonemic awareness doesn't stop being relevant after second grade, and this webinar makes that case well.

resources.title: LINCS
resources.description: A national site for adult education practitioners with free self-paced online courses and a searchable resource collection. It also has a Learner Center that connects adults to free online resources for reading and job skills.

resources.title: Free Webinars for Tutors and Teachers
resources.cost: Free, some need a free account
resources.description: Recent topics include the updated citizenship test, teaching foundational reading skills to adult ESOL learners, health literacy, and moving from ESL to employment. Some resources on the site need a free account.

resources.title: Money Smart for Adults
resources.description: An instructor-led financial education curriculum with 14 modules. Each one comes with an instructor guide, slides, and a participant guide you can download. Other languages, including Spanish, are available through the FDIC catalog.

resources.title: Free Reading Resources for Beginning-Level, US-Born Adult Learners
resources.cost: Free, some need a free login
resources.description: A short roundup of free reading practice for adults who grew up speaking English and are building basic reading skills. It points to Reading Skills for Today's Adults, ReadWorks, and Newsela Lite. ReadWorks and Newsela Lite need a free login, and ReadWorks was made for kids.

resources.title: Adult Learner Persistence Project
resources.description: Findings from 18 adult education programs that tested ways to keep learners coming back. It includes strategies for intake, instruction, support, and program design, self-assessment tools, and six "drivers of persistence."

resources.title: The Literacy Cooperative
resources.description: A Cleveland nonprofit working to advance literacy through a service delivery system that meets the highest standards in the field. Its vision is that all children and adults in Greater Cleveland reach their highest literacy potential.

resources.title: Literacy Opportunity Fund
resources.description: Grants for U.S. nonprofits that teach adults directly. Funds can cover general operating costs like salaries, technology, and supplies, or a specific project or new program.

note.label: Good to know
note.text: You need to be a registered 501(c)(3) with an EIN. Book distributions and lending libraries are not funded. The 2026 round closed October 1, so watch for the next one.

resources.title: Mobile Learning Fund
resources.description: Free licenses to online learning tools for adult literacy programs, including New Readers Press Online Learning, Learning Upgrade, EnGen, Leamos, and News for You Online.

note.label: Good to know
note.text: Applications are open year round and awarded on a rolling basis while funds last. Learners must be 16 or older. You will need to complete a free demo or trial, and it does not cover devices.

resources.title: Adult and Family Literacy Grants
resources.description: Grants of up to $10,000 for adult and family literacy. Nonprofits, public libraries, and schools or colleges that provide direct literacy services can apply.

note.label: Good to know
note.text: Your organization must be within 15 miles of a Dollar General store. The 2026 adult and family deadline was in early February, so expect an early-year window.

resources.title: Innovation Grants
resources.description: Grants for programs that find successful and innovative ways to reach more learners. Any program listed in the National Literacy Directory can apply.

note.label: Good to know
note.text: The page does not post award amounts or dates, so check with the directory. Getting your program listed first is the way in.

resources.title: DigitalLearn
resources.description: A free online hub for digital literacy training. Short, video-based courses with narration on using a computer, navigating websites, email, and internet privacy. Available in English and Spanish.

note.label: What we love about it
note.text: Clean, accessible, and easy to navigate. The self-paced format works well for learners.

resources.title: Learning Chocolate
resources.description: A free vocabulary learning platform organized into themed categories like body, community, food, jobs, and transportation, with picture dictionaries and audio pronunciation. Learners can choose from multiple language interfaces.

note.label: What we love about it
note.text: Easy to use, visually clear, and fun. There's no login required. Learners can just jump in.

resources.title: Life Skills for Adult Learners
resources.description: A free interactive online course covering practical life skills, including workplace readiness, communication, financial literacy, and navigating everyday situations. Self-paced and mobile-friendly.

note.label: What we love about it
note.text: The mobile-friendly format means learners can use it on their phones, a real advantage for busy adults juggling work and family.

resources.title: USA Learns
resources.description: A free website where adults can learn English, build job skills, and prepare for U.S. citizenship. Lessons cover speaking, listening, reading, writing, grammar, pronunciation, and life skills, and they work on a phone, computer, or tablet.

resources.title: Find an Adult Education Class Near You
resources.description: Ohio Aspire is the state's adult education program network, with local programs run by schools, colleges, libraries, and nonprofits. The state's Aspire page and program directory show which program serves your county.

resources.title: National Literacy Directory
resources.description: A searchable directory where literacy and education programs list themselves, so adults and volunteers can find classes and tutoring near them.

resources.title: Bow Valley Readers
resources.description: Seven levels of stories written for adults, each with an audio track so learners can listen along while they read.

resources.title: Ohio's Diploma Options for Adults
resources.source: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce
resources.description: One page that lays out the ways Ohio adults can earn a high school diploma or equivalence: the Adult Workforce Diploma Program, High School Equivalence (formerly GED), the High School Continuation Program, and Aspire.

note.label: Good to know
note.text: The Adult Workforce Diploma Program opened July 1, 2026 and is no cost to adults. The 22+ Adult High School Diploma Program and the Adult Diploma Program no longer take new students.

resources.title: Khan Academy
resources.description: Free videos, practice exercises, and progress tracking that learners can use at their own pace on a phone, tablet, or computer. It covers all four High School Equivalency areas: math, language arts, science, and social studies.

note.label: Good to know
note.text: Everything is free except Khanmigo, the AI tutor, which needs a paid subscription for learners.

resources.title: VOA Learning English
resources.description: News stories read about one-third slower than normal speed, with captions, audio, and text. It also has lesson series for beginners (Let's Learn English) and for advanced learners (American Stories, Everyday Grammar).
